subject: Polity
stem: Which of the following statements about the joint sitting of Parliament is CORRECT?

options.option_text: It is presided over by the President of India
It is presided over by the Speaker of Lok Sabha
It is presided over by the Chairman of Rajya Sabha
A joint sitting cannot be held for Constitution Amendment Bills

explanation: Under Article 108, a joint sitting is presided over by the Speaker of Lok Sabha (or, in absence, the Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha). Joint sittings can be called for ordinary Bills (not Money Bills or Constitution Amendment Bills) when there is disagreement between the two Houses.

subject: Polity
stem: The total strength of the Rajya Sabha, as provided in the Constitution, shall NOT exceed:

options.option_text: 200 members
238 members
250 members
275 members

explanation: Article 80 fixes the maximum strength of Rajya Sabha at 250 — 238 elected from States/UTs and 12 nominated by the President for their expertise in literature, science, art, and social service. Present strength is 245.

subject: Polity
stem:
Consider the following about Parliamentary privileges in India:
1. They are available only to individual members, not to the House collectively.
2. Courts cannot inquire into the proceedings of Parliament.
3. Freedom of speech in Parliament is an absolute immunity.
Which of the above is/are CORRECT?

options.option_text: 1 only
2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3

explanation: Parliamentary privileges belong both to each House collectively (right to punish for breach) and to individual members. Courts cannot inquire into proceedings under Article 105(2), making Statement 2 correct. Freedom of speech is NOT absolute — it doesn't protect disclosures of secret proceedings of the House.

subject: Polity
stem: The 'Zero Hour' in Indian Parliament refers to:

options.option_text: The first hour of parliamentary business reserved for Starred Questions
The time immediately after Question Hour when members raise matters of urgent public importance without prior notice
The period when Parliament debates the budget grants
The final session of Parliament before dissolution

explanation: Zero Hour is an informal device that begins right after the Question Hour ends (i.e., around 12 noon — hence 'zero hour'). Members raise matters of immediate public importance without prior notice. It is not mentioned in the Constitution or Rules of Procedure; it evolved out of parliamentary practice.

subject: Polity
stem: A Money Bill introduced in Parliament can be introduced ONLY in:

options.option_text: Rajya Sabha, with Lok Sabha concurring
Lok Sabha, on the recommendation of the President
Either House, but requires joint sitting for disagreement
Lok Sabha, without any Presidential recommendation

explanation: Under Article 109, a Money Bill can be introduced only in Lok Sabha and only on the recommendation of the President. Rajya Sabha can suggest amendments but cannot reject it; Lok Sabha may accept or reject Rajya Sabha's suggestions. If not returned within 14 days, the Bill is deemed passed by both Houses.

subject: Polity
stem: The Speaker of Lok Sabha is elected by:

options.option_text: All members of Parliament (both Houses)
Members of Lok Sabha alone
The President of India on the advice of the Prime Minister
Members of Lok Sabha by proportional representation with single transferable vote

explanation: Article 93 provides that Lok Sabha shall, as soon as may be, choose two members to be Speaker and Deputy Speaker respectively. They are elected by simple majority by members of Lok Sabha alone. The President has no role in the election.

subject: Polity
stem: Which of the following Parliamentary Committees is NOT a Standing Committee?

options.option_text: Public Accounts Committee
Estimates Committee
Select Committee on a Bill
Committee on Public Undertakings

explanation: PAC, Estimates Committee, and Committee on Public Undertakings are Financial Standing Committees — they are permanent and reconstituted annually. A Select Committee (or Joint Select Committee) is an Ad Hoc Committee constituted for a specific Bill and ceases to exist once that Bill is passed.

subject: Polity
stem: Under which Article of the Constitution does Parliament have the power to legislate on a State subject during a National Emergency?

options.option_text: Article 249
Article 250
Article 252
Article 253

explanation: Article 250 empowers Parliament to legislate with respect to any matter in the State List while a Proclamation of National Emergency (Article 352) is in operation. Article 249 covers legislation on State subjects when Rajya Sabha passes a resolution in national interest; Article 252 is for two or more States requesting Parliament to legislate; Article 253 is for implementing international treaties.

subject: Polity
stem: The Rajya Sabha CANNOT be dissolved because:

options.option_text: Its members enjoy life-tenure in the House
It is a permanent House — one-third of its members retire every two years
Only the Supreme Court can dissolve Rajya Sabha
It requires a constitutional amendment to dissolve it, which has never been passed

explanation: Rajya Sabha is a permanent House under Article 83(1). It is never dissolved as a whole. One-third of its members (who serve 6-year terms) retire every two years, ensuring continuity of the House at all times. Lok Sabha, by contrast, can be dissolved by the President.

subject: Polity
stem: Prorogation of Parliament differs from Adjournment in that:

options.option_text: Prorogation terminates a session; all pending business lapses except pending Bills
Adjournment terminates a session; prorogation only suspends a sitting for a day
Only the President can adjourn Parliament; the Speaker can prorogue it
Prorogation and adjournment have identical effects on pending business

explanation: Prorogation (by the President under Article 85) terminates a session. Pending notices, motions, and resolutions (but not Bills or Select/Joint Committee reports) lapse on prorogation. Adjournment merely suspends the work of the House for a specific time — pending business resumes at the next sitting. The Speaker adjourns; the President prorogues.
